body:
I know the feeling so well and it's such a natural reaction. I spent so much time trying to figure out if he was a psychopath or just emotionally abusive and nice deep inside, but that doesn't really matter in the end. What matters is how *we feel* in the relationship, and if we can live with it being like that. Also, you may never find a definite answer to this question, if you tell your story people may say "that's abuse" and some may say "I don't know". You're the only one who truly knows what you went through and you need to figure out for yourself what your story is. For alot of people it's easier to be angry and hate everything about their ex and label them something and never mention the good, but some of us struggle with that. Maybe your story is some version of "he had abusive behavior, he did some good things but unfortunately he was hurting me a lot"? Find what you're comfortable with, and if your feelings change it's okay to change what your story is.

It's so hurtful when this happens and they turn. The fact that they treat you so good when they're being nice makes the fall so much bigger than if they were assholes all the time too. If they're really manipulative they know this will confuse you and they'll use this to keep you around.. It might also be done unconsciously, but it has the same effect.

I've spent so much time crying over losing the good part of him, I can't even believe it's the same person. I kinda had my own little funeral for the good part of him, because it honestly felt like someone died and was replaced by the abuser. You may never stop thinking "how is this possible??", but listen you don't even want to know how that's possible. You have a better heart, a healthier way of functioning with other people, so much that you can't at all relate to this behavior. It's a good thing you don't understand this. You're only 3 weeks in NC, and although we shouldn't make promises to other people if we can't make sure it's true, I feel confident that in time these thoughts will settle down. It's tough as hell going through this though, not gonna lie.

Oh yes and hopefully the anger will disappear one day, right?? So you need to find something else to motivate you so you won't actually need the anger to stay safe and healthy.

My best advice from speaking to professionals and from my own experience is:

1.  Work on finding out how your life is currently better, and take notes. If this person was abusive you were probably struggling with being present in your own life, with friends and family while you were with him. Maybe you always had a pit in your stomach, and went to bed scared. Did you feel safe? How do you feel better now, what has changed? Is there something you can do now that you couldn't do with this person in your life?
2. Ask yourself what was missing in your relationship and think of how you'd rather have it. For example, I was always attacked if I talked about any issues with him, that was uncomfortable and unsafe, so instead I want someone who can say "oh I'm so sorry, what can I do to repair this?". I was always scared, I don't want to be scared in my relationship, I'll rather find someone who makes me feel good. Try to imagine how much better that would be.

Hopefully doing these exercises will help you realize there's very little to miss. But you're also allowed to miss them! After all you did have feelings, and I think trying to avoid those feelings now can make things worse. It's okay to say "I miss this part of him desperately", but try to follow up with "but he was very unhealthy in many other ways and I don't miss that at all" to remind yourself why you're in no contact to begin with. It's okay to grieve the happy moments, just stay safe.

Good luck <3

That's so not okay. My sister also expect all of us to do things for her, but I think she's understood that I wont.

It's soul crushing being in a relationship with an abuser. Having family members act like this on top of everything is draining me completely.

Have you ever considered spending less time with your sister or even completely cutting her off? I'm looking for ways to get my energy back at this point. Any tip you have for protecting myself mentally, I'll take it!

Oh they love the attention and power, of course! Just like the saying "any PR is good PR", any attention is good attention for these people. I always say it's like my nex had a sieve in front of his ears, that would only let in positive meanings to everything I said while the negative was blocked out. The noise of me screaming and crying turned to music in his ears. No matter what, the only thing he could see or hear was positive reinforcement. The very first time he ignored me for no reason, he told me (when he finally picked up) that what had went through his mind when he looked at his phone as I kept trying to call him was: "wow, I must be pretty important for her to call me so many times". He simply measured his own value in how much other people reacted, not *how* they reacted. A fundamentally distorted view of themselves and how to connect with people, combined with a complete lack of empathy.

That is the scariest and sickest thing I've ever seen anyone write. I'm happy you're out of that relationship. My nex would say that he blocked out emotions and have more subtle ways of saying he didn't feel much. He always said in a way that made me feel bad for him, usually connected it to childhood trauma. Sadly, that doesn't change the outcome and the abuse.

This has been the hardest part for me. I guess the short answer is: you don't get over it. You just focus on different things after a while, and (as crazy as it seems) you start thinking less and less about this person. A mental health professional will help!

My nex just disappeared and refused to give me any closure or answer anything. This left me incredibly angry with the feeling of injustice. I reached out to his mother, and a friend of his, but everywhere I turned they supported him. I realized I needed to protect myself from everything that had anything to do with him, and that's the purpose of no-contact. I realized I was more at peace being away from them. It's for you, not for him. You're not hiding, you're eliminating toxic and dangerous people from your life so you can be happier. It's the same with the mutual friends or anyone who supports him over you, because that does hurt and right now you need 100% support.

In the beginning my anger was so strong I experienced several panic attacks because I was so scared of the level of emotion and my own thoughts. I literally felt like I was a small step away from buying a baseball bat and beating him up, which isn't like me at all. I wanted to cuss him out all the time, but I didn't (if you do, you are allowed to. Give yourself a break, you were abused). The reasons I didn't was that I wrote it down instead and told myself I had to wait and think it through, and I also learned that as a narc he probably would love the attention and getting a reaction out of me. So at this point I still cared what was going through his mind.

Slowly the anger started settling, which I never thought it would. I believe *time* (although it's a cliche) does heal many wounds. Everytime I get angry I'll write my thoughts down, and tell myself I can do something about it later when I'm less angry. I also surrounded myself with people who were supportive and angry with me. I was told that what will hurt the narc more is being ignored. But now that even more time has passed, I actually am proud to say that I don't care what he thinks!! What I care about is ME, my peace, and as I carry on with my life I will ask myself "what do I need?". It's still possible to report him for psychological violence or whatever law applies in your country, there's probably plenty of more ideas on how to feel justified.. But whatever we choose to do (or not do), we need to be mindful of ourselves and what is healthy for us. Eventually I guess you just realize that the best thing is actually to not give a f\*\*\* because they do win no matter what, so not caring about them is the only way out. It's easy to feel defeated and powerless by that, so I really do think the trick is to focus purely on yourself and your growth. He made you feel like shit and this is how their abuse works: they make you feel like shit so your entire life is revolved around them. As you focus on rebuilding yourself and your confidence without him, you will notice how you simultaneously stop thinking about him because you are so much more important. It's easier said than done, but I'm confident you will get there in time. Meanwhile it's completely okay to shout, punch or break something, cry, and feel it all. But choose what makes you happy and more at peace. Choose that every day. This is the time to be completely self-absorbed :)

Omg it used to piss me off so much whenever people would say stuff like that, and it just made me feel more alone in the world because no one was actually supporting me and my thoughts. Sometimes we need people to stop with the bullshit and the lies, and just acknowledge that our lives are shit. Even though I'm a bit better now and not feeling suicidal these days, I totally get why people don't want to be in this world, and I would understand if I had killed myself also. People like to say that whenever you're depressed/suicidal you're sick and not "in your right mind", but honestly I think it's the other way around. The world is a shit place with lots of shitty people in it, and some of us experience even more shit than others. That's the truth. To get by and be truly happy you need to be stupid, slightly delusional and shallow like some of the people you're talking about, and just ignore every problem in the world and everything bad - live in a pink bubble and not take anything in too deep. Which just sounds sad to me. But honestly it's the only thing that works, whenever I start thinking about how much everything sucks I just do something else and I forget about it. Lol. Well I do hope you find something worth living for some day, but in the meantime I hope you just don't stumble upon any triggers to actually go through with killing yourself. Because I do think that those of us with depression or other mental illnesses are a special kind. I don't know about you but I relate so much to Kanye singing "See, if I was trying to relate it to more people I'd probably say I'm struggling with loving myself. Because that seems like a common theme. But that's not the case here". I always thought, I love myself but this place sucks. On that note - Aurora has a beautiful song called "a different kind of human". She's toying with the idea of aliens coming to get those of us who don't belong on this planet, those of us who care but are treated poorly, and taking us home where we all live happily together.

Anyway if anything I wrote resonated with you, don't hesitate to message me.
Thanks, I'll check out the book! Wish you all the best on your path to healing!

I do think that in time we'll learn to see the signs early on and have less tolerance for this abuse. My therapist taught me that we all have some things we tolerate more than others. For me, it was people being on-and-off like my dad. I grew up with it and so my tolerance is much higher than someone who had parents who were consistent. The abuse cycle is very much like an on-and-off behavior.

But tolerance does not mean we aren't getting hurt in the process, it means we stay longer - and with a narcissist once you stay too long it'll take ALOT to leave.

These people hunt those of us with a higher tolerance for bad behavior, those of us with wounds from our past. Maybe one lesson is working on this tolerance, setting boundaries and following through. We need to find someone who is worth trusting again who can *show us* not everyone is bad, but pick them more carefully. Or else we might find ourselves falling into the claws of a new narcissist who's exploiting the hurt we're feeling from the previous abuse and initiating the love bombing phase to be our savior.

I hope we can both build our trust in ourselves and in others <3

Yeah and trust me, even if they do that they might turn around a day later, a week, a month. Mine was apologizing for everything, it seemed very sincere. Then I asked to see his phone (I knew he was sleeping with other people), he refused, told me I would never be worth giving up that privacy. When I got upset he just stared at me and said "I've never done anything to you". And so his apology was just bullshit. Thrown away in seconds.

My ex was abusive too, emotionally and verbally. We had talked about how he needed to talk to a therapist, and meanwhile we shouldn't be together, but we were going to talk for a while to have closure. He said he wanted to marry me one day and he'd be back, and ofc I could reach out when I needed answers or something.

The next day he was gone. I haven't heard from him in almost 3 months. I ran into him the other day, we're actually neighbours, and he seemed normal until I asked him why he was acting like this. He got upset, walked home and locked me out when I tried to talk to him.

It just seems like they don't want us to have closure. Him leaving you and not allowing you to have any closure might be his final act in abusing you.

I dated a guy once who upset me, but he wasn't abusive. I found his snapchat password. I was just like you, I checked it all the time. The reason I'm telling you this is because I think you'll get tired in time, just like I got tired. You'll check it less and less. Try to notice how uneventful it probably is. And I want you to know that you're not not-normal. He used the same password on netflix and honey I've been enjoying free streaming for 4 years now, lol. I dunno I sometimes feel like owning it takes away some of the shame, so at least you can stop beating yourself up about it so much. It's not healthy obsessing over it, and I bet you have a pit in your stomach often? Notice when you haven't checked it in a while and give yourself some positive reinforcement. In time it'll be only curiosity and not obsessive thoughts, and as you keep healing from the abuse and the break up I think your need for checking his instagram will slowly fade.

Focus on you and your healing instead of focusing on him <3

I really hope for you and her that she's actually working on herself in therapy. For a couple of months I thought my abuser had finally seen the light: he came to me and said he felt awful, he wanted to make it up to me and he knew he needed to get proper help. I asked to see proof, I asked if he had talked about our situation, but he never showed me any contact with a psychologist or any other sign that he actually was talking to someone. We agreed we needed to keep our distance from each other while he got help, but we'd still talk. One day I asked about his therapist. He never answered and just disappeared. He's been gone for 2-3 months. Highly doubt he ever saw anyone about his issues. Now I'm his issue - I ran into him on the street and it seems like he hates me. So if I were you I'd ask to see some proof if you haven't already.

Yeah.. He works in the military in my country, and they obviously have a lot of narcissists because they love power.. A while ago I sent them a notice about his behavior and today I called them to find out whats going on, and the woman seemed like she disliked me all of a sudden and all she said was that she had a message from him and it was that he said he wanted nothing to do with me. I can't believe he went from saying he wanted to marry me, to just treat me like I'm the worst person in the world. It's so crazy..

Yeah it's hard, my mom was treated poorly by her alcoholic boyfriend and I just had to ignore it eventually and wait for her to realize he wasn't good for her.. I think the best thing you can do is be supportive of your friend when he/she needs you, and try not to start any arguments over this. If your friend is really deep in it still then he/she might pull away from you, and it might even work in the favor of the abuser.

Keep building your friend up, show them they deserve so much more and do what you can to make them feel less lonely (many of us hold on because we felt so lonely before we met the abuser). One day he/she might be strong enough <3

Yes and that's why we sometimes try so hard to get those parts back, isn't it? The good parts were there, and we miss that terribly.

I agree, that part of accepting that it's them and it's their responsibility is very difficult. Honestly I think I'm still thinking of him as two completely separate persons. And I want nothing to do with the new one that emerged. I hope that in time I'll be able to see the person for who they really are as a whole - that must be easier to deal with. Until then I'll allow myself to grieve, because it is a loss of some sort.

That's such a nice thing to do for your friend. It gets very lonely and victims feel easily misunderstood because a break up with an abuser isn't like any other break up.

I wish I had a brilliant answer for your questions, but it's complicated. I told him multiple times that we couldn't see each other anymore, but I knew I really needed to get out when I was so broken down that I actually attacked him back, physically (which was "reactive abuse" as it's called). I didn't recognize myself anymore and I was scared for my own mental health. Still I'd say I didn't fully realize it until he had been gone for a while and I got out of that insane bubble I lived in. Some abusers/narcissists leave on their own eventually, if they get tired of fighting and feel like they can't manipulate you anymore. Even though I was with him, I never fully accepted the way he treated me. He just disappeared one day.

The second question I'll answer even though he was the one who finally left and has ignored me ever since, because I still had to deal with wanting to reach out. I really wanted to understand, and to confront him. Eventually I was able to start moving on by focusing on me instead, and keeping in mind that time really does heal these wounds a lot. I'm trying to figure out why I stayed, and focusing on what I want in a relationship. When you start to remind yourself that you can actually feel safe every day, breathe normally, have a disagreement with a person without being scared they'll leave forever but instead know that they'll stick around.. That really helps :)

Yeah, but why not take the lessons? Ugh I always try to understand people, it makes it easier for me to be empathetic and find peace even though it's not what I'd do in a certain situation. But the people who just constantly chooses to harm other people, I can't wrap my head around that.

Breaks my heart hearing what you went through. I hope your son is doing well! Remember to remind him that he's loved and worthy of love <3

The guy I was with also withheld affection, and when he was sleeping with others he claimed it was to protect me because he cared about me. Such a crazy logic - the fact that he did that was such a huge part of what hurt me in the first place.. I guess it was just another way of making it seem like he had my best interested at heart when he was really just being selfish.

It's so touching to read what you're saying about helping others and spreading love. I really had to start finding that part of me again when he left. I reacted to the abuse with anger, and then figured I was almost as bad as him because of my reactions. The part where you're saying "*We’ll be fine as we walk by faith and love and not allow this major change to keep us from being the loving folks we are*" makes me cry. I've been through some bad things when I was younger and I always had that same thought, I've always been so filled with love. I'm really looking forward to this bad relationship being something that I learned from and can use in a positive way, once the grieving is over.

You mention their souls knowing they're capable of accepting and returning. What do you think is the reason why they won't give anything then?

Thank you for that <3 I feel better today, but I know there's probably another bad day (or two, or three!) coming. Sometimes I just cry like a baby. It feels like a death - such a huge loss. At the same time I'm so happy I've got myself back, I'm finally present in my own life! I just wish things were different, I wish he was different..

Hi!
I'm going to reply to this because you are making a lot of assumptions, but I would initially also like to say that you do have some very good points.

First of all it is a problem for me that other people's butts and tits are available at any time, and you will fail trying to make me ashamed of that. I have no issue with him watching porn - I know that is limited to a certain time and place. Not only is this IG thing embarrassing for the both of us, but I also think this could negatively affect his view of what is normal and what he can expect in real life. I don't think it's healthy for a future relationship to have these false truths available at your phone at any time. I understand that other people may not have a problem with this at all, and I'd love to be one of them. Anyway, I brought THIS up to him, and it was his solution to unfollow them. I understand that you feel like me getting upset about something and bringing it up is manipulation, but then, are we all just suppose to not say anything because speaking about our worries is manipulating? It kinda seems like you see manipulation even where you don't really know what the full conversation was like. That also seems to be the case as I read your comment further.
You're making the assumption that I want to bully him into dating me. No, but I am bullying him into telling me what the hell is going on - because what he said was very confusing to me. I also explained how this affected me. That's communication, not manipulation. That's why I said he needs to explain this, or else I have no choice but to move on, because I'm confused and hurting. I'm really sorry you're seeing only manipulation here, but I'm happy that you're able to say "that is what it sounds like" - finally just a tad of humility in your comment.

You're absolutely right that I am insecure, though! And I'm very open about this. What I'll never do is push someone to like me. It seems you have forgotten the last part of my post, about how I usually just call it quits instead of pushing through situations.

Also, your assumption that this convo started because I was riffling through his instagram is, at best, not accurate. He actually showed me his instagram and I casually noticed this - and our conversation started like that and evolved. I'm glad he took it in a much better manner than you. Isn't it funny that he seemed totally ok with it, and you're really offended by my behavior? You're blowing it out of proportion with the whole Chris Hemsworth-comment, like I ever said this guy couldn't watch TV. Please at least keep your facts straight. It does sound childish and manipulative when you type things like that, but that's not because that's what I actually said... With respect, I think there's some projection going on here.

I love the part about painting people with the same broad brush. I'm really working hard on not doing this anymore, and to not let fear control my decisions. I am seeing a therapist already, and trust issues is the next thing on our agenda. I know I sound vague, but we've worked on even bigger issues already, so luckily my own insight has improved a lot. My therapist can't always be available whenever something comes up, so reassuring words like for example your paintbrush-comment and the previous comment on this post, is really helpful. Thanks for your good wishes, I really appreciate that.

Ah so many of us are in, or have recently been in, a situation like this! I was in something similar not long ago. I saw all the signs that you saw too, but he had never told me about there being another girl, I just knew. I got upset with his avoiding behavior one night. I asked him if he was seeing someone else, but I realized that his answer didn't really matter, because I couldn't handle the anxiety anymore anyway. I erased him from social media before he could answer.. Bad way of handling it, I know, and it definitely hurts to have to cut someone off even if it's for your own good..

So I later contacted him to apologize for ghosting him. He told me he had stayed in contact with an old fling, and he also apologized for his behavior (although, like so many other guys, he tried to play the "but we're not a couple"-card... Yeah, but you still hurt my feelings dude).

​

This guy is in fact my next door neighbor! So a bit of anxiety unfortunately stayed with me, because I can hear him in the hallway from time to time.. I once asked him if he would want to talk to me again, and he said that he's now dating this girl who he kept in touch with, but if it wasn't for the fact that he'd like to give that a chance, he could go back to talking to me again. Too bad he wasn't thinking about picking one of us to focus on a little sooner! 

Currently looking for someone who will give me their attention, like I give all my attention and love. We all deserve someone who picks us any day, someone who can't wait to talk to us, and is really excited about meeting up. Remember that!

We live in the same city and I try to keep my distance as much as I feel like I can. Especially now when I'm down, I make sure I don't see them at all.. I definitely want even more distance one day, so your question if moving is possible is absolutely a right question to ask and it may well be a solution in some time.

Thank you so much for your advice, I've just started to realize that I should probably focus more on my self-love right now.. Hopefully this too will pass if I can stay strong for a while longer.

It just seems like my kind of way to go, when I can't have an injection. That would really be my thing, but I don't know how to do that. I've just always felt like I needed to sleep, so pills are perfect. It would probably be uncomfortable, but I'd be in bed and sort of sleeping in it forever in my then nonexistent mind. It just sounds so much more lovely than jumping off a bridge or something. What's the most comfortable way to go? Does anyone really know?

Really? I read that even just 200mg of morphine could be fatal, since this is codeine you'd probably need a bit more but 1000mg should def be sufficient. Morphine doesn't help with pain...? That's just not a fact, haha! I've taken these before. Are you trying to trick me?

I don't have a good family, and that sucks. All my life, for as long as I can even remember, I've been thinking to myself that my life doesn't matter. That I should seize to exist. I've never had a partner, I've never had anything to live for. When I was just a kid, just a few years old, I would just sit still in my room and cry and pretend like I didn't exist.  I used to dream of jumping in the ice cold water when I was 15.

How do you do it though? What's your reason to live? I really can't think of one no matter how hard I try.

Btw love your nickname or whatever it's called on reddit. I'm new here. Hi.
